title: Midnight at Northstar
overview: Northstar Clinic's scheduling system was encrypted overnight and a ransom note appeared. The clinic has offline backups, but a small set of records was accessed first.
objective: Identify the likely entry point and determine whether the incident was external opportunism or enabled by a compromised staff account.

hypotheses.statement: An outside attacker used a stolen vendor account whose credentials were exposed in a phishing message.
A clinic employee intentionally encrypted the system to disrupt operations.

evidence.title: Incident timeline
evidence.content: Scheduling workstations became unavailable at 12:14 AM. The ransom note requested payment in cryptocurrency.

evidence.title: System access overview
evidence.content: The last privileged login used a vendor support account. No staff badge entry was recorded after 9 PM.

evidence.title: Authentication audit
evidence.content: The vendor account authenticated from a new overseas address using a password-only login. Multi-factor authentication had been disabled during a support call.

evidence.title: Helpdesk phishing report
evidence.content: A technician reported a convincing vendor password-reset email received two days earlier. The message linked to a lookalike support portal.

evidence.title: Endpoint review
evidence.content: The encryption process was launched remotely through the vendor management tool. No local executable or staff USB activity was found.

suspects.name: Unknown external actor
suspects.role: Likely operator using a compromised support account

suspects.name: Clinic IT technician
suspects.role: Recipient of a suspicious password-reset email

witness_statements.statement: They received a password-reset email that appeared to come from the support vendor.

timeline.event: A technician received a lookalike vendor reset message.
The vendor support account authenticated from a new address.
